label: Flint 39.8B-A2.5B Q4_K_M, one llama-server per B70, every weight in VRAM, q8_0 KV, -np 2 per card, conversation-affinity proxy; replay agent-long-16
engine_build: mainline llama.cpp SYCL >= b11803 (F16-overflow expert-activation scaling workaround)

files.note: bartowski Q4_K_M, 25,346,651,360 bytes; header read into data/models/flint.json

conditions.engine_flags: llama-server -ngl 99 -fa on -c 262144 -np 2 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 -ub 2048 -b 2048 --jinja --metrics --cache-reuse 256, one container per card (:8101, :8102), dp-affinity-proxy :8090

src: lane flint-1030 launch line, read from odie's process table (read-only) 2026-10-30; spec from the GGUF header and config.json
note: Prediction written before any replay of this build; see data/predictions-flint-1030.json. Every input not READ or MEASURED is an ASSUMPTION and says so.

resident_plan.stall_src: READ: llama-server batches prompt chunks and decode tokens into one step (continuous batching), so a read delays the decode of the other slot

instances.src: one llama-server per B70 (:8101, :8102) behind dp-affinity-proxy :8090: a conversation sticks to one card, new conversations split evenly

slots.src: -np 2 per server: at most two turns decode together on a card; with -c 262144 each slot holds 131,072 tokens

warmup_s.src: ASSUMPTION: the lane replays as the rows did (agent-replay --warmup-s 600 --duration-s 600)

layers.src: config.json num_hidden_layers 49 (2 dense + 47 MoE); GGUF block_count

experts_used.src: GGUF header expert_used_count 6 (+ 1 shared, counted in dense_read_gb)

dense_read_gb.src: data/models/flint.json intake: all tensors read each token except routed experts and the token_embd lookup: attention 0.983 + output 0.327 + shared experts 0.314 + router 0.099 + dense FFN of layers 0-1 0.080 GB

experts_all_gb.src: data/models/flint.json intake: routed expert tensors (q4_K / q5_K / q6_K / q8_0 mix), all 256 x 47 layers; one token reads 6/256 of them = 0.544 GB

file_gb.src: GGUF file size; a 2048-token prompt chunk touches every expert, so each chunk reads the whole file once

kv_bytes_per_token.src: config.json: 14 full-attention layers x 4 KV heads x (K 128 + V 128) x 1.0625 B (q8_0) = 15,232 B per context token read per decoded token. The 35 sliding-window layers read 513 cells each (~19.5 MB a token, < 2 % at 80k depth): left out

kv_read_eff.src: ASSUMPTION (high leverage at depth): SYCL flash-attention decode reads q8_0 KV at half the effective weight-read bandwidth. Range 0.3-1.0. No llama.cpp SYCL depth sweep of a GQA model on the B70 in the ledger

depth_tokens.src: agent-long-16 prompt_tokens median 81,724 (agent-replay stats, as data/predictions-fit-in-vram-1027.json inputs.agent_depth_tokens)

read_tokens.src: a read's fresh tokens incl. re-read: R8's measured mean per read 2,187 at 1 agent and 1,202 at 16 (data/predictions-fit-in-vram-1027.json inputs.read_mix); P barely moves with it (one chunk either way)

out_ratio.src: ASSUMPTION (before any run): the recording's own output lengths, as the turn model's table gave it at 10:52Z (no Flint replay, models.flint.out_vs_recorded empty). Pinned in the recipe when data/workload.json took the measured flint-1030 rows, so the frozen prediction reproduces

reread_per_turn.src: ASSUMPTION (before any run): about one -ub 2048 chunk a turn back to the last context checkpoint, between strata's measured 708 (R8 n1) and vLLM align mode's measured 2,396 (Ornith n1); range 300-6,000. The turn model's llamacpp-sycl-slots-swa row held it at 10:52Z; pinned in the recipe when that row took the measured flint-1030 values, so the frozen prediction reproduces

decode_anchors.src: MEASURED: runs/bench.jsonl, mainline llama.cpp SYCL b11706 (f74e2fa6a), one B70 (4c:00.0), llama-bench tg128 short prompt, every weight resident: two MoE models fit t = read_gb x a + layers x c, giving ~563 GB/s effective and ~0.113 ms a layer of launch cost. Older build than b11803 (INFERRED: same kernels apart from the overflow workaround)

engine_slowdown.src: ASSUMPTION: the b11803 F16-overflow expert-activation scaling workaround's stated 10-30 % slowdown, midpoint, applied to every weight-read and launch term (decode) and to the linear prefill term. Range 1.1-1.3

batch_layer_mult.src: ASSUMPTION: two tokens in one step (two slots) cost 1.25x the single-token launch time per layer (SYCL mmvq/MUL_MAT_ID handle up to 8 columns with their small-batch kernels: lab notes). Range 1.0-1.6

linear_ms_per_token.src: ASSUMPTION (high leverage): prefill weight math per token. vLLM XPU measured 0.128 ms on a 3B-active MoE with every weight resident (data/predictions-fit-in-vram-1027.json inputs.m_ms_per_token); x 2.5/3 active, x 2 for llama.cpp SYCL MUL_MAT_ID against vLLM's kernels (no Flint or llama.cpp-SYCL resident-MoE prefill ubench yet). Range 0.10-0.40

attn_ms_per_token_per_ctx.src: ASSUMPTION (highest leverage at 80k depth): vLLM XPU's 2.9e-6 ms per token per context token on a model with 10 full-attention layers of 4,096 query width (data/predictions-fit-in-vram-1027.json inputs.attn_s_per_token_per_ctx_token), x 1.4 for Flint's 14 such layers, x 2 for llama.cpp SYCL flash attention against vLLM's. At 80k this is 0.65 ms a token, about 70 % of a read. Range 4e-6 to 1.6e-5
